questions.title: Mathematics clubs management system
questions.text: There is a network of mathematics clubs that has commissioned the development of a comprehensive system. The system needs to automate numerous administrative tasks and manage student records, grades, attendance, teacher schedules, and reports.

parts.title: Mathematics clubs management system (a)
parts.text: Describe **three** reasons why interviewing would be the most effective method to gather information from the mathematics clubs to build the management system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Allows for in-depth conversations with club administrators/teachers/staff/experts (1)
Creates a more tailored/bespoke/custom system / Makes sure that the system meets the exact needs (1)
Helps to clarify the details of how the mathematics clubs currently operate (1)
Allows to ask follow-up questions (1)
Truthful / reliable answers/information due to face-to-face conversation from club administrators/teachers/staff/experts (1)
[Max: 3] Accept any other reasonable answers.
scheme.model_answer:
1 It allows in-depth conversations with the club administrators and teachers.
2 Follow-up questions can be asked to clarify how the clubs currently operate.
3 The system can be tailored to the exact needs of the clubs.

parts.title: Mathematics clubs management system (b)(i)
parts.text: Describe **three** advantages of using the Waterfall model for the given scenario.

scheme.mark_scheme:
The outcome is predictable due to fixed requirements agreed at the start / Final product closely matches the original requirements (1)
Predictable time / Strict deadline that allows accurate project timelines (1)
Clear documentation as each phase produces well documented artefacts (1)
Strict adherence to initial requirements / Requirements do not change during development (1)
Easier for project management as each stage has specific deliverables and a review process / simple to track progress (1)
Fixed budget as total cost can be accurately estimated (1)
Suited for projects with requirements well-defined from the beginning (1)
[Max: 3] Accept any other reasonable justifications.
scheme.model_answer:
1 The requirements are fixed at the start, so the final system closely matches what the clubs asked for.
2 Each stage has clear deliverables and documentation, so progress is easy to track.
3 The time and budget can be estimated accurately.

parts.title: Mathematics clubs management system (b)(ii)

parts.title: Mathematics clubs management system (b)(iii)

questions.title: Tuition fees
questions.text:
After analysing the clubs' operations, the following rules for calculating tuition fees were identified:

1. Tuition fees are calculated based on a student's grade:
   - Students in grades 7-9: 15,000 tenge per month.
   - Students in grades 10-12: 18,000 tenge per month.
2. If there are more than 6 students in a group, the manager applies a discount of 10% to the tuition fee.

parts.title: Tuition fees (a)
parts.text: Create a flowchart to calculate the annual tuition fee for a student in a group.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Flowchart elements:
• Inputs (grade, groupNum) (1)
• Output (fee, error message) (1)
• If blocks (check grade) (1)
• If block (check discount) (1)
• Loop back to the start (1)
• Correct declaration of fee (15000, 18000) (1)
• Correct calculation (annual fee) (1)
• Correct calculation (fee with discount) (1)
[8]
Accept other correct flowchart. Do not award marks for wrong shapes of the elements.

points.criterion: Loop back to the input for an invalid grade

scheme.model_answer: START → INPUT grade, groupNum → IF grade >= 7 AND grade <= 9 THEN fee = 15000, ELSE IF grade >= 10 AND grade <= 12 THEN fee = 18000, ELSE OUTPUT "ERROR" and loop back to the input → fee = fee × 12 → IF groupNum > 6 THEN fee = fee × 0.9 → OUTPUT fee → END
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept other correct flowcharts. Do not award marks for elements drawn with the wrong shapes (decision = diamond, input/output = parallelogram, process = rectangle).

parts.title: Tuition fees (b)(i)
parts.text: Create a Level 1 Data Flow Diagram (DFD) to calculate the annual tuition fee for a student in a group.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Level 1 DFD elements:
• Entity(s) (manager is required) (1)
• Processes (calculate tuition fee, apply discount) (2)
• Data store (1)
• Defined data flow (1)
[5]
Example: manager —grade, number of students→ Calculate fee —value of fee→ D Results of fee —value of fee→ Output fee —value of fee→ manager.

Accept other correct notations of DFD and correct solutions; accept other correct entities, data stores and processes which satisfy the scenario and logic.
Do not award marks for wrong shapes, or for violation of the rules:
1. Entity can't be related directly to another entity
2. Entity can't be related directly to data store
3. Data store can't be related directly to another data store
4. All data flows must be labelled
5. Data flows can't be bidirectional
6. All processes and storages should have both incoming and outgoing data flows
7. All data flows must have directions
scheme.model_answer: Manager —grade, number of students→ (1 Calculate fee) —value of fee→ [D1 Results of fee] —value of fee→ (2 Output fee) —value of fee→ Manager
scheme.ai_instructions: Do not award marks for wrong shapes or violations of DFD rules (entity–entity, entity–store, store–store, unlabelled, bidirectional or undirected flows, processes/stores without both input and output).

questions.title: Database concepts and normalisation
questions.text: To facilitate efficient management of the mathematics clubs operations, a database has been created.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (a)(i)
parts.text: Define the term *table* in the context of a database.

scheme.mark_scheme:
A table in a database is a structured collection of data organized into records and fields / tuples and attributes (1)
Collection of structured records / set of tuples and attributes / set of fields and records (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: A structured collection of data organised into records (rows) and fields (columns).

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (a)(ii)
parts.text: Describe how an attribute applies to a record in a table.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Each attribute has a name / data type (1)
One characteristic of one specific object/record (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: An attribute stores one characteristic (property) of the object that a record describes.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe how indexes can optimise the management of the mathematics clubs system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
An index allows the database to locate specific records quickly / without scanning the entire table (1)
An index is a reference that allows quick access/search to data stored in a table (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: An index lets the database find specific records quickly without scanning the whole table.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (b)(i)
parts.text:
Database normalisation is an important process that helps organise data efficiently and minimise problems with storage and processing.

A table of students and their classes is provided.

| StudentName | TutorGroup | TeacherName | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| Asyl Arman | 10A | Ms.Aila, Mr.Erasyl | MathExamPrep, MathematicalModeling |
| Leila Aman | 10A | Mr.Erasyl, Mr.Ernar | SAT, Geometry |
| Rauan Asem | 10B | Mr.Erasyl, Mr.Ernar | SAT, Geometry |
| Almir Talant | 11A | Ms.Aila, Mr.Erasyl | MathExamPrep, MathematicalModeling |

Identify and explain **two** features of the table that do not satisfy first normal form (1NF).

scheme.mark_scheme:
1. Non-atomic values (1)
TeacherName, StudentName and Class columns contain multiple values in a single cell / Some fields do not contain a single, indivisible value (1)
2. No primary key (1)
There is no unique identifier for each record (1)
[4]
Accept candidate and secondary key. Accept explanation only related with the given example table.
scheme.model_answer:
1 Non-atomic values
Explanation: TeacherName and Class contain several values in one cell, e.g. "SAT, Geometry".
2 No primary key
Explanation: there is no field that uniquely identifies each record.
scheme.ai_instructions: Explanations must relate to the given table.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (b)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the fields that make the composite primary key.

scheme.mark_scheme:
StudentName, Class [1]
Accept StudentName, TeacherName
scheme.model_answer: StudentName, Class
scheme.ai_instructions: Accept StudentName + Class, or StudentName + TeacherName.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (b)(iii)
parts.text: Define the concept of *partial dependence*.

scheme.mark_scheme: Partial dependence occurs when a non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite primary key rather than the entire key. [1]
scheme.model_answer: When a non-key attribute depends on only part of a composite primary key, not on the whole key.

parts.title: Database concepts and normalisation (b)(iv)
parts.text: Identify an example of partial dependence in this table.

scheme.mark_scheme:
TutorGroup depends only on StudentName (1)
TeacherName depends only on Class (if composite keys are StudentName, Class) (1)
[Max: 1]
scheme.model_answer: TutorGroup depends only on StudentName, not on the whole key (StudentName, Class).

parts.text: Write an SQL query to create table CLASS (ClassID, Subject, IsOnline, TeacherID).

scheme.mark_scheme:
CREATE TABLE CLASS (1)
(ClassID INT PRIMARY KEY, (1)
Subject VARCHAR(100), (1)
IsOnline BOOLEAN, (1)
TeacherID INT, (1)
FOREIGN KEY (TeacherID) REFERENCES TEACHER(TeacherID) (1)

parts.title: Mathematics clubs database (b)(iii)
parts.text: Write an SQL query to display the first names of all students who attend the class with ClassID equal to 101.

scheme.mark_scheme:
SELECT STUDENT.FirstName (1)
FROM STUDENT, CLASSGROUP (1)
WHERE STUDENT.StudentID = CLASSGROUP.StudentID (1)
AND CLASSGROUP.ClassID = 101; (1)
OR
SELECT STUDENT.FirstName (1)
FROM STUDENT (1)
JOIN CLASSGROUP ON STUDENT.StudentID = CLASSGROUP.StudentID (1)

FROM STUDENT
JOIN CLASSGROUP ON STUDENT.StudentID = CLASSGROUP.StudentID
WHERE CLASSGROUP.ClassID = 101;

parts.title: Alarm system logic (a)(i)
parts.text:
A security system is designed to activate an alarm. The alarm is triggered when either a door sensor detects an opening or a motion detector registers movement, but only if the system is armed.

The specifications for the three input subsystems are given below:

- Door Sensor: A (Open = Logic 1)
- Motion Detector: B (Movement = Logic 1)
- System Armed Switch: C (Armed = Logic 1)

Write the Boolean expression for the output Alarm System (Q) based on the inputs A, B, C.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Q = A.C + B.C
OR
Q = (A + B).C
[Max: 1] Accept other correct notations.
scheme.model_answer: Q = (A + B) · C

parts.title: Alarm system logic (a)(ii)
parts.text: Complete the truth table for the logic system.

scheme.mark_scheme:
Q: 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1 (rows 000 to 111)
[2] 1 point for four correct lines in the Q column.

parts.title: Alarm system logic (a)(iii)
parts.text: Describe how the value of the System Armed Switch (C) affects the output Q.

scheme.mark_scheme:
When C is 0, regardless of the values of A and B, the output Q is 0 / Whenever C = 0, Q = 0 (1)
When C is 1, if either of the values of A and B equals 1, the output Q is 1 / When C = 1, and A = 1 or B = 1, Q = 1 (1)
[2]
Allow similar answers using the terms Door Sensor, Motion Detector, System Armed Switch.

points.criterion: C = 1 → Q = 1 if A or B is 1

scheme.model_answer: If C = 0 the alarm never sounds (Q = 0) whatever A and B are; if C = 1 the alarm sounds when A = 1 or B = 1.

parts.title: Alarm system logic (b)(i)
parts.text:
Simplify the following Boolean expression. Show your working.

Q = (X · ¬Y) · (Z + X · ¬Y)

scheme.mark_scheme:
Distributive law: Q = X·¬Y·Z + X·¬Y·(X·¬Y) (1)
Idempotent law: Q = X·¬Y·Z + X·¬Y (1)
Absorption law: Q = X·¬Y·(Z + 1) ⇒ X·¬Y·1 ⇒ X·¬Y (1)
[3]
Award 1 mark for the correct answer.
scheme.model_answer:
Q = X·¬Y·Z + X·¬Y·X·¬Y   distributive
= X·¬Y·Z + X·¬Y           idempotent
= X·¬Y·(Z + 1) = X·¬Y      absorption
scheme.ai_instructions: Show-working question: award marks for the laws applied; award 1 mark for the correct final answer X·¬Y if the working is missing.

parts.title: Alarm system logic (b)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a logic circuit for the simplified expression.

scheme.mark_scheme:
NOT gate on Y (1)
AND gate with X and ¬Y producing Q (1)
[2] Award full marks only for correct order of logic gates.
scheme.model_answer: Y → NOT; X and the NOT output → AND → Q
